title: Add a lean JSON profile that drops empty and default fields
lead:
Every `--json` read ships full-fat: `short_title` duplicates `title` when unset,
`path` is an absolute string, `trees_literal` is internal, and empty collections
(`notes`, `flags`, `depends_on`) and empty-string fields (`pass`, `group`, `reason`)
are all emitted. Roughly 35% of a `list --json` row is empty scaffolding, and because
JSON sits in context and is replayed every turn, the waste compounds across a session.
A lean profile shrinks `list`/`next`/`show` by an estimated 30-45% with no change to
what the agent can learn.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The agent pays for every byte of every read on each subsequent turn until compaction.
Omitting fields that carry no information is a pure, passive credit saving that needs
no change to the agent's behavior.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
`src/slicer/cli.py` (a `--lean`/`--full` flag or a config default for `--json`),
`src/slicer/model.py` (the `to_dict` shaping), `docs/agents.md` (document the shape).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a lean shaping applied under `--json`: omit empty lists, empty strings, and
default-valued internal fields (`trees_literal`); omit `short_title` when it equals
`title`; omit `path` unless requested. Gate it behind an explicit flag (or a config
default with `--full` to opt back) so the documented shape stays stable — the error
contract is `code`-based, but the success shape is documented and must not silently
change. Apply uniformly across read commands.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Under the lean profile, a `next`/`list`/`show` payload omits empty and default fields
and the duplicated `short_title`/`path`; a test measures the byte reduction on a known
fixture and asserts no informational field is lost. Full mode reproduces today's shape
exactly. The change is documented in `docs/agents.md`.
